statement: Audit the index compiler: its hash-prefix width, the magic string that names the index format, and the entry and turn-index classes it builds.

steps.prompt: Read `ptr_engine/compile.py` and list the top-level classes it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/compile.py` and report the value of `HASH_PREFIX_LEN`.
Read `ptr_engine/compile.py` and report how many top-level functions it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/resolve.py` and report the value of `DEFAULT_MAX_REFS`.
Read `ptr_engine/resolve.py` and report how many methods the class it defines has.
Read `ptr_engine/annotate.py` and report the value of `DEPTH_ROOT`.
Read `ptr_engine/annotate.py` and report the value of `DEPTH_LEAF`.
Read `ptr_engine/pointer_table.py` and report how many top-level functions it defines.
Compare the hash-prefix width you found in `ptr_engine/compile.py` at step 2 with the number of top-level functions in the same file at step 3 and say which is larger.
Read `ptr_engine/store.py` and report how many top-level functions it defines.

final_question: Using the constant you identified at step 2 — do not restate it — report the string value of the constant in the same file that names the index format.

checkpoints.question: What is the value of `DEFAULT_MAX_REFS` in `ptr_engine/resolve.py`?
What is the value of `DEPTH_LEAF` in `ptr_engine/annotate.py`?
